items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'a guy named McCarthy in England, has written a book about jazz' and Interviewee does not claim any personal interaction or relationship with him.

ctx.x: Well, Teddy, we'll just get back onto you, then. We were talking about Charlie Elgar, which was one of the band leaders, a violinist. And I think he was probably one of our greatest black historians because Charlie kept records of everything, all the teachers of the big bands and all the bands of that era. And I remember this book that I think I mentioned to you once before, a guy named McCarthy in England, has written a book about jazz. And he's got the most extensive one that I've seen on the territory bands,…

Somewhere I've got a picture of that Speed Webb band, which was operating the same time as Trent. Zach White's band, I've seen pictures of that group. And Frank Terry, the Chicago Nightingales, do you remember that group?
